observations: Vintage-style portable sewing machine, orange/rust colored body, metal construction.
Brand name 'RICCAR' visible in white text on the machine body in photo 0.
Three control dials and a thread spool pin visible on top in photo 0.
Power cord and a separate foot pedal visible in photos 1 and 2.
White plastic/fiberglass carrying base or case visible under the machine in photos 1 and 2.
Machine is resting on a wooden table/counter surrounded by fabric bolts, suggesting a tailoring shop setting.
No power outlet, plug socket, or the machine running/stitching is shown in any photo.
Some faint wear/scuff marks visible on the orange paint near the handwheel and base in photo 1.

claims.evidence: No photo shows original packaging, receipt, or an unused/pristine finish; faint wear marks are visible in photo 1 which is inconclusive either way.

claims.claim: Implied fully functional (by virtue of being 'never used')
claims.evidence: No photo or clip shows the machine powered on, needle moving, or a stitch sample produced.

risks.risk: Machine may not power on or motor may be seized/faulty, common in older unused machines left in storage.
risks.proof: A short video of the machine plugged in, foot pedal pressed, needle moving and producing a stitch on fabric.

risks.risk: Missing accessories (bobbins, extra needles, manual, power cable condition) that affect usability.
risks.proof: A close-up photo of the accessory box/case contents and the power cord end/plug.
risks.if_unproven: priced as base unit only, no accessories

risks.risk: Electrical safety of an old cord/plug, visible wiring looks exposed in photo 0.
risks.proof: Close-up photo of the plug and full cord length for fraying or exposed wire.

risks.risk: True age/model of the Riccar unit is unclear, affecting whether it's a basic straight-stitch or multi-stitch machine, which changes value.
risks.proof: Photo of the model/serial plate, usually on the back or underside of the machine.

proof_requests: Video of the machine running (foot pedal pressed, needle moving, stitching a scrap of fabric).
Close-up of the serial/model plate on the back or bottom of the machine.
Close-up of the power plug and full cord for wear.
Photo of any included accessories (bobbins, manual, extra needles) laid out.
response.reason: The item is clearly identifiable as a Riccar portable sewing machine from visible branding, but the 'never used' and implicit working-condition claims are unverifiable from photos alone, so it must be priced at worst case as not confirmed working until a functional video is provided.
